title: 2026 New Mexico Gubernatorial Election
description: The 2026 New Mexico gubernatorial election will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the next governor of New Mexico. Incumbent Democratic Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term, making this an open-seat race. Former U.S. Secretary of the Interior Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, defeating Bernalillo County District Attorney Sam Bregman with 72% of the vote, and will face Republican nominee Gregg Hull, the former three-term mayor of Rio Rancho, in the general election. The race will test whether Democrats can maintain control of the governor's office in a state that has trended Democratic in recent presidential elections but faces ongoing challenges around crime, economic diversification, and education outcomes.
polling_note: No general election head-to-head polls (Haaland vs. Hull) were found as of mid-2026. The only recent public poll identified was an Emerson College/KRQE News 13 survey from April 2026 which focused on the primary matchups and did not test a general election scenario.

candidates.name: Deb Haaland
candidates.summary: Deb Haaland is the Democratic nominee for governor of New Mexico in the 2026 election. She served as U.S. Secretary of the Interior from 2021 to 2025 under President Joe Biden, becoming the first Native American cabinet secretary in U.S. history, and previously represented New Mexico's 1st congressional district in the U.S. House from 2019 to 2021. A member of the Pueblo of Laguna, Haaland has centered her campaign on affordability, healthcare access, public safety reform, and environmental protection.

candidates.name: Gregg Hull
candidates.summary: Gregg Hull is the Republican nominee for governor of New Mexico in the 2026 election. He served as mayor of Rio Rancho from 2014 to 2026, becoming the city's longest-serving mayor, and oversaw a period of rapid growth in New Mexico's third-largest city. A small businessman before entering politics, Hull has campaigned on a platform of public safety, economic growth, education reform, and infrastructure investment.

forecast.rationale: This is an open-seat race with no general-election head-to-head polling available, which materially increases uncertainty. Still, the available race context gives Democrats an edge: New Mexico has trended Democratic in recent presidential elections, Democrats currently hold the governorship, and Deb Haaland enters the general election as a prominent statewide figure after serving as U.S. Secretary of the Interior and winning her primary decisively. Gregg Hull appears to be a credible Republican nominee with executive experience as Rio Rancho mayor, so the race is not out of reach for Republicans, especially in an open-seat contest centered on crime, the economy, and education. With no direct general-election polling, this forecast relies primarily on state partisan lean, candidate profile, and the overall race description rather than measured voter preference.
